claims.claim: Raw evaluator, label and gold-answer fields are excluded from the online Guard projection; exact_gold exposes only a derived authorization object.
claims.boundary: This is an implementation and experiment-contract claim, not evidence that other published systems leak evaluator fields.

claims.claim: Unsafe effects in the four main DeepSeek authorization cells remained at or near the observed floor.
claims.observed: Three cells were 0/100 and policy-only plus auto_compiled was 1/100; all paired unsafe-effect Holm-adjusted p values were 1.0.
claims.boundary: A near-floor endpoint does not prove universal robustness and limits power to distinguish mechanisms.

claims.claim: Changing from auto_compiled to exact_gold reduced benign-tool task completion under both Guard variants.
claims.observed: Policy-only changed from 22/60 to 9/60 (-21.67 percentage points); M3-full changed from 16/60 to 7/60 (-15.00 points).
claims.boundary: The exact_gold condition is an oracle-sensitivity treatment, not a recommended deployment policy.

claims.claim: Exact authorization changed runtime burden by removing ASK while increasing DENY incidence, failures and tail latency.
claims.observed: ASK incidence fell to 0; DENY incidence was 48.89% for policy-only and 45.00% for M3-full; failure incidence was 23.89% and 24.44%; p95 latency was 19.42 and 19.62 seconds.
claims.boundary: ASK and DENY are record-incidence measures; event totals are reported separately.

claims.claim: The evaluated provenance, temporal/data-flow and confirmation extensions did not show a stable independent benefit over policy-only.
claims.observed: Under auto_compiled, M3-full had 0/100 versus 1/100 unsafe effects but completed 16/60 versus 22/60 benign tool tasks; Public Pro and Flash both placed M3-full above policy-only in unsafe effects.
claims.boundary: The result is limited to the tested implementation, policies, benchmarks and DeepSeek models; it is not proof that provenance is generally ineffective.

claims.claim: The unfavorable M3-full versus policy-only security direction is observed in both DeepSeek V4 Pro and V4 Flash Public matrices.
claims.observed: Public Pro recorded 38/600 versus 13/600 unsafe effects; Public Flash recorded 24/400 versus 12/400.
claims.boundary: This supports a within-provider model replication only and does not establish cross-provider generalization.

claims.claim: Authorization-regime outcomes are reported separately for AgentDojo and M3-v2 and by prespecified M3-v2 attack family.
claims.boundary: These strata are descriptive heterogeneity analyses; they are not independently powered confirmatory tests.

claims.claim: Defense-aware adaptive search found additional first unsafe effects between budgets 50 and 200.
claims.observed: First unsafe effects were found for 4/40 tasks by query 50 and 18/40 by query 200.
claims.boundary: Two budget points do not establish saturation and no budget-500 or budget-2000 claim is allowed.

claims.claim: The lean DeepSeek experiment retains official returned-model identity, response IDs when obtained, ITT failures, token/cost accounting and isolated-effect execution without provider tools or real external actions.
claims.boundary: Provider model aliases do not identify an immutable hidden-weight revision.

claims.claim: The authorization findings generalize across DeepSeek and Gemini providers.
claims.boundary: The three-Pacific-quota-day rule closed at 32/450 terminal work items. The incomplete subset remains diagnostic and cannot support cross-provider generalization.

claims.claim: M3 is the first, only, state-of-the-art or universally superior provenance-aware runtime defense.
claims.boundary: VIGIL, DRIFT, Task Shield, Progent, IPIGuard, CaMeL, ARGUS, AuthGraph, FAVA and provenance-sensitivity auditing occupy overlapping mechanism and evaluation space.

claims.claim: JISA is SCIE and JCR Q2 on the submission date.
claims.unlock_condition: An authorized institutional user must verify current SCIE coverage and JCR quartile immediately before submission.

claims.claim: The 21 references currently cited by the manuscript have verified metadata, stable landing pages and publication status; 11/21 principal citation contexts were explicitly checked against official abstracts or proceedings summaries.
claims.boundary: The context review is a 52.4% structured sample, not a claim that every sentence of every cited paper was independently reproduced. Review any newly activated citation and repeat publication-status checks at submission.
